top_story: Trump’s claim on 3 August that Iran talks will begin after he canceled a major strike collides with Tehran’s flat denial hours earlier, exposing a volatile gap between coercive signaling in Washington and diplomatic consent in Tehran after six months of war. That uncertainty is sharpening rather than easing regional instability, as Israel has moved to intensify deadly operations in Gaza despite the US-backed plan Trump promoted on 31 July as a breakthrough, while still leaving core sequencing questions unresolved on withdrawal and Hamas disarmament. The same pattern of political impunity is visible in the occupied West Bank, where settlers established at least six new outposts after the 27 July killings amid raids, assaults, and demolitions backed by military presence. The emerging picture is of US diplomacy failing to translate into restraint on the ground, leaving civilians in Gaza and the West Bank to absorb the costs of widening Israeli action and unresolved US-Iran brinkmanship.
